transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-13 16:00 UTC; Duration ~53m; Redwood: Maya/Devon/Lin; Crestmore: Anika/Jonas/Priya/Mateo

Summary: quick check-in on contract extension path and capacity uplift for EU private deployment; main asks: compliance artifacts, staging access, clarified SLAs for p95 latency and sustained throughput. Customer leaning toward Dedicated/EU-private but worried about cost and failover. Agreed next steps to share SOW, SOC2, spin up staging cluster and run throughput sanity run.

Topics: contract extension timeline; EU private (VPC) provisioning; latency vs cost tradeoffs; KV cache / prefix caching; KMS/HSM for keys; audit logs and retention; pilot success criteria and go/no-go dates.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: okay, hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick check-in, we've got about 50 minutes. want to run through where we are on the EU-private pilot, plus extension terms and what crestmore needs to greenlight the uplift.
[00:19] Anika: hey Maya, thanks. short context — we've been testing Redwood hosted for the last six months in us-east and it's been stable; now the product team wants EU private for residency and an expected 2x increase in qps in Q3. main blockers are compliance sign-off and a predictable burn rate.
[00:37] Jonas: yeah, and to add — we have latency SLOs for patient-facing features (p95 < 300ms) during peak. curious about how Redwood handles KV cache warming and if that will affect p95 on cold start.
[00:52] Devon: great question. so our serving runtime has a couple levers — continous batching, prefix/KV cache and model variants. on EU-private we'll pre-warm KV cache for the model variants you pick; there is still some cold-penalty on first megabatch but for steady state p95 should be well under 300ms for the gpt-like 8k sequence profiles you described. caveat: depends on batch windows and how many small requests you have.
[01:20] Mateo: small interruption — what's the difference operationally between Redwood Dedicated and Private? we keep hearing both.
[01:26] Maya: yeah so quick — Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in Redwood's hosted infra with tenancy guarantees; Private is the VPC/on-prem option where control plane is private and you run in your AZ or our private tenancy in EU zone. Private gives you stronger residency and network controls. Dedicated is simpler and faster to onboard but doesn't provide the same level of network isolation.
[01:45] Priya: for compliance, we need SOC2 plus the recent pentest summary. also KMS integration — keys must be customer-managed. we also need audit logs retained for at least 12 months and the ability to export them.
[02:01] Lin: right, we can share SOC2 and pentest. KMS is supported — we do HSM-backed KMS or bring-your-own-key via standard APIs. audit logs are exportable and can be forwarded to your SIEM; retention policies are configurable. i'll drop links.
[02:18] Anika: good. timeline wise, product wants a staged rollout: EU staging in april for integration tests, pilot for a month, then prod in june if OK. does that timeline look feasible?
[02:29] Devon: feasible. we'll need a week or two to provision EU-private staging once we get a signed SOW and network details. there is also a short window to validate KMS and RBAC. for the pilot we'll recommend load tests simulating 2x traffic and a 2-day soak.
[02:45] Jonas: cost — can you show the delta between hosted token rate, dedicated reserved rate, and EU-private run-rate for our projected qps?
[02:53] Maya: yes, we'll include a 3-tier option in the SOW: conservative uplift, expected 2x uplift, and high-growth 3x. we'll show committed monthly vs on-demand and the unit economics with and without quantization suggestions.
[03:09] Anika: one more technical: when you route requests in failover (say eu region degraded), does Redwood fall back to US-hosted model or another variant? we need to understand data residency implications of fallback.
[03:21] Devon: by policy — routing is configurable. we can set a strict no-cross-border fallback for compliance, in which case requests queue or return 5xx with a defined policy. alternatively, you can allow fallback to a geo-compatible model in EU hosted zone only. for strict sovereignty you'll want the no-fallback policy. that's a tradeoff: strict gives you compliance but increases outage surface.
[03:44] Priya: that's important. we likely need the strict no-cross-border fallback for patient data, but can consider limited fallback for non-PHI endpoints. we'll map endpoints.
[03:55] Maya: noted — action item for mapping endpoints to data classes.
[03:59] Jonas: operational question — what's the expected lead time to add a new EU region cluster if we want to expand further?
[04:06] Devon: typical lead time is 2-4 weeks for a new geocluster in EU with Dedicated/Dedicated-plus Private; depends on GPU availability but we can pre-reserve. there is also a provisioning checklist we'll provide.
[04:19] Mateo: regarding metrics — we'll need token-level cost breakdowns, per-route latency, and error traces accessible. can we get access to the console for read-only pre-provision?
[04:30] Lin: yes, we'll provision RBAC view-only for your SRE and compliance for the staging cluster. also we'll give a sample dashboard with token cost breakdown and p95 heatmaps.
[04:43] Anika: on the pilot success criteria — we propose: sustained p95 < 300ms for 7 of 7 days under 2x load, error rate < 0.1%, and no compliance findings in KMS integration. does that align?
[04:56] Devon: that's reasonable. we'll add model-quality checks for hallucination rates on your eval set if you want.
[05:03] Jonas: yes please, include eval gating.
[05:07] Maya: ok recap and timeline: Crestmore wants EU staging in April, 30-day pilot May, prod June. we will send SOW with three price tiers and a phased MSA amendment. Lin will share SOC2/pentest. Devon will provision EU staging after SOW signed. next meeting to align on failover policy and endpoint classification.
[05:25] Priya: small nit — can we get the SOW to review legal redlines at least two weeks before signing?
[05:30] Maya: yes, we'll aim to send the draft SOW by next Friday.
[05:34] Anika: and can we run a short AB of quantized model vs full-precision in staging to evaluate quality delta? that will affect cost decision.
[05:43] Devon: absolutely — we can bake that into the pilot plan and collect output metrics.
[05:48] Jonas: any competitors you recommend we watch? we've got proposals from BigCloudAI and HydraInference; curious how Redwood compares on unit cost and failover.
[05:58] Maya: quick callout — BigCloudAI has aggressive discounting but less transparent p95 guarantees; HydraInference's private offering was more ops-heavy. Redwood emphasizes production observability and clear cost levers (batching, KV cache, quant profiles). we'll include a short comparison in the SOW appendix.
[06:15] Lin: i'll also attach an ops-runbook and the provisioning checklist.
[06:20] Anika: thanks all.
[06:22] Maya: great, final recap of action items in chat and we'll follow up with links.

Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: automated notes — occasional mis-heard terms ("KV cash" -> KV cache, "Redwood Dedi" -> Redwood Dedicated), speaker overlaps, minor punctuation issues.
